label: Late copy steps of short (L=3/4) sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, never on original tokens or <DEL>. It depends mostly on position and sequence length. In L=3 sequences it fires on the 2nd and 3rd outputs (t=4,5; precision about 0.73 in that cell), with the largest activations on the final output. In L=4 sequences it fires on the 3rd output (t=6). Weaker clusters elsewhere: L=9 at recall_idx 3 (t=12) and the last output (t=17), plus scattered steps in L=6-8. Within these positions, whether it fires depends on token identity: inputs u and 2 give the strongest activations (the top examples are almost all u/2 inputs in L=3 sequences), and I found no simple token rule. It does not fire on the first output (recall_idx 0), on L=4 recall 1 or 3, or on L=5. The predicate captures about 75% of activation mass on dev, but precision is only about 0.38.
